newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY TO REOPEN CONSULATE IN ROMANIA.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY TO REOPEN CONSULATE IN ROMANIA.

text.p: Hungary has decided to reopen in Romania a consulate which had been closed by the Romanian communist dictator Ceausescu, a government spokesman said on Thursday.

"(The government) decided to open the Hungarian consulate in Cluj and to enable Romania to open a consulate in Szeged (southern Hungary) or elsewhere in the country," Prime Minister's Office Secretary of State Elemer Kiss told a news conference.
He added that the two countries will also open honorary consulates in the Romanian Black sea port of Constanta and the western Hungarian town of Gyor.
The announcement is part of a process of warming of relations between the two countries which have traditionally been strained over the rights of Romania's 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians.
Bilateral ties have improved steadily since Romania's November general elections ousted President Iliescu and two the party of ethnic Hungarians joined the new government coalition.
Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin announced in Budapest in December that the new government of his country no longer opposed the reopening of the Cluj consulate.

Earlier this week, Hungary and Romania set up a joint military unit and signed accords on the protection of military secrets and cooperation in tackling organised crime, drug trafficking and terrorism.
